name: Operation Open Strait
summary: Hypothetical scenario: Iran has closed the Strait of Hormuz to shipping. US Navy and Marine forces land on Kharg Island, secure its oil terminal intact, clear the shipping lanes and escort tankers through so the world sees the supply line open again.

states.objective: Briefing: the Strait of Hormuz is closed to shipping. Take Kharg Island with its oil terminal intact, then reopen the strait.
Fly Raven over both landing beaches and mark the defences before the landing craft go in.
Choose the landing beach. North is close to the oil terminal but heavily defended; West is quieter but the Marines reach the airstrip first.
Marines land on the north beach. Secure the beachhead.
Push straight into the oil terminal and secure it without damaging the jetties, tanks or pumps.
Take the airstrip so helicopters can operate from the island.
Marines land on the west beach. Secure the beachhead.
Take the airstrip first so helicopters support the push on the terminal.
Secure the oil terminal without damaging the jetties, tanks or pumps.
Kharg Island secured. Hold it while the fleet moves to the strait.
Clear the inbound and outbound shipping lanes: drones find the hazards, clearance teams remove them.
Escort the tankers through the strait. Every tanker that gets through shows the world the supply line is open.
Debrief: how much oil is flowing and what state the terminal is in.
The strait is open, the terminal is intact and the tankers are through. The world sees the supply line restored.
The strait is open, but the terminal was damaged or too few tankers got through. Supply is only partly restored.
The operation failed: the beachhead was lost or no tanker got through. Restart from the last checkpoint.
